newsitem.title: USA: Intruder entered U.S. Moscow compound - report.
newsitem.headline: Intruder entered U.S. Moscow compound - report.

text.p: A Russian man in military fatigues entered the U.S. Embassy compound in Moscow earlier this month and managed to break into the home of the top-ranking American diplomat in Russia where he spent the night, the Washington Post reported on Thursday.
The man was discovered the next morning naked in the envoy's shower, the newspaper said.

Quoting diplomatic sources at the embassy, the Post said the man was detained by security personnel and identified himself as a Russian army deserter. After a brief interrogation, he was turned over to Russian authorities.
The sources told the Post the incident, which took place over the weekend of March 8-9, prompted an intensive security review of the compound.

Of the 120 residential units in the compound, the man chose to enter Townhouse One, the home of American charge d'affairs in Moscow, John Tefft, and his wife, Mariella. As charge d'affairs, Tefft is, in effect, the acting ambassador because President Bill Clinton has not yet appointed a successor to the previous ambassador Thomas Pickering.

The newspaper said there was no indication the intruder gained access to the more sensitive chancery building, where diplomatic business is conducted and highly classified materials are located. Nor was there any known evidence to suggest the man was spying.
